blocks.prompt: 1 Design Thinking looks at problems from different angles. Explain its five steps (Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, Test) using the book's example of designing a new school bag. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
Design Thinking is a method that helps us look at problems from different angles; instead of jumping to solutions it first understands the problem deeply.

1. Empathize: put yourself in someone else's shoes to understand their feelings, needs and challenges. Bag example: talk to students to learn what they like and dislike about their current bags.

2. Define: after gathering information, clearly define the problem. Bag example: 'Students need a lightweight, durable, and spacious bag that is comfortable to carry'.

3. Ideate: brainstorm all possible solutions without worrying if they are perfect. Bag example: a bag with extra padding for comfort, or one with compartments that make it easy to organize books and supplies.

4. Prototype: a prototype is a simple version of your idea that you can create quickly. Bag example: a basic model made of cardboard, fabric or even paper to show what it might look like.

5. Test: test the prototype to see if it works well. Bag example: ask students to try the bag and give feedback; based on their comments, make improvements until you have a final product that solves the problem.

blocks.prompt: 2 A good business plan has several key parts. Explain the Executive Summary, Business Description, Market Analysis, Organization and Management, Products or Services, Marketing and Sales Strategy and Financial Plan, giving an example of each from the book. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
A business plan is a document that describes your business idea, how you plan to make it successful and the steps you will take to achieve your goals.

1. Executive Summary: a brief overview of the business idea: what the business does, its goals and how it plans to achieve them; a summary of the plan's most important points.

2. Business Description: explains what the business is about: products or services, target customers and what makes it unique. Example: a lemonade stand selling refreshing lemonade in the neighborhood; or 'Our chai dhaba will offer freshly brewed chai ... near the local bazaar.'

3. Market Analysis: shows you understand your market: potential customers, their needs and competitors. Example: for pet-sitting, find how many pet owners are in the area and what other services exist.

4. Organization and Management: how the business will be organized, with team members and roles. Example: a school club's president, secretary and other roles.

5. Products or Services: what you sell or offer, with features and benefits. Example: how tutoring lessons will help students improve their grades.

6. Marketing and Sales Strategy: how you will attract and keep customers; marketing methods and sales tactics. Example: a crafts business using social media and local fairs.

7. Financial Plan: financial goals and how to achieve them; budget, funding needs and expected revenue. Example: if you need $100 for supplies, explain how you will raise it and what you expect to earn.

book_ref.quote: A good business plan usually has several key parts

blocks.prompt: 3 Digital tools make creating a business plan more accessible and efficient. (i) Explain how business plan software helps, with the book's online bookstore example. (ii) Explain how collaborative tools help a team, with the book's bakery example. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Business plan software: several software solutions simplify creating a business plan. They provide structured templates, financial modeling features and guidance that help you develop a clear and detailed plan.
Example: to start a small online bookstore, you use software like PlanGuru or Enloop and select a template tailored for retail businesses. The software guides you through sections like the business overview and market analysis. Its financial calculators let you input costs for inventory, website development and marketing; it then generates financial projections, such as estimated sales and cash flow, with charts and graphs. This simplifies presenting the plan to investors or applying for funding.

(ii) Collaborative tools: team collaboration is essential, especially with partners or advisors. Collaborative tools let multiple people contribute to the plan simultaneously, with real-time feedback and revisions.
Example: you open a bakery with a friend skilled in baking while you handle operations. Using Google Drive or Dropbox Paper, both of you work on the same document at the same time: your partner writes the products and recipes section while you develop the marketing plan and financial forecast. Commenting and suggestion modes let you leave feedback or propose changes without altering the original text, so you decide together even if not in the same place. Version control features track changes and let you revert to earlier drafts if necessary.

book_ref.quote: Below, we discuss the software that can help you create your business plan

blocks.prompt: 4 Market research gathers data about the market in which a business operates. (i) Explain qualitative and quantitative research with the book's examples. (ii) Explain customer surveys and focus groups with the bakery examples. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
Market research is the process of gathering data about the market in which your business operates, to understand customer needs, preferences and behaviors and the strengths and weaknesses of competitors.

(i) Qualitative research focuses on understanding the underlying reasons, opinions and motivations of customers. It collects non-numerical data through interviews, focus groups and observations. Example: before opening a bakery, in-depth conversations with potential customers about their preferred breads and pastries show what customers value most, informing products and marketing messages.
Quantitative research collects numerical data that can be measured and analyzed statistically; it is useful for identifying patterns and trends in customer behavior. Example: a survey on how often people buy coffee and how much they will pay helps set prices and predict sales volumes.

(ii) Customer surveys are a powerful tool for gathering information from a large number of customers, online, over the phone or in person. A series of questions gives data on preferences, behaviors and demographics. Example: a survey of the neighborhood before opening a bakery finds which baked goods people want, when they are most likely to buy and how much they will spend, so products and business hours can be tailored.
Focus groups are a small, diverse set of individuals brought together for detailed discussion about a product, service or concept, to understand customer opinions and attitudes. Example: participants sample breads and pastries and discuss likes, dislikes and suggestions, giving valuable qualitative data for refining products.

book_ref.quote: This data can help you understand customer needs, preferences, and behaviors

blocks.prompt: 5 After gathering market data, the next step is to analyze it. Explain understanding trends and patterns, market segmentation, competitor analysis and predictive analysis, with the bakery examples, and say how they lead to data-driven decisions. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
Analyzing market data means reviewing the information to find patterns, trends and insights that guide business decisions and turn data into useful strategies.

1. Understanding trends and patterns: a key objective is to identify trends and patterns. Example: a survey of bakery purchases shows most purchases occur on weekends, so marketing or special promotions on weekends can increase sales.

2. Market segmentation: breaking a larger target market into smaller, more specific groups based on age, income or buying habits. Example: younger customers prefer sweet pastries while older customers favor whole-grain bread; adjusting products and marketing for each group improves satisfaction and sales.

3. Competitor analysis: studying competitors' strengths and weaknesses, pricing strategies and customer feedback to find ways to differentiate your business. Example: if a nearby bakery is popular for artisanal bread, add gourmet pastries or seasonal cakes to attract a different group.

4. Predictive analysis: using historical data to forecast future trends and outcomes. Example: if sales show a steady rise in demand for a product, predict it will continue and increase production or expand the menu; this reduces risks and maximizes opportunities.

Data-driven decisions: the primary aim is well-informed decisions on choosing products, setting prices and planning marketing. Example: an underperforming product is discontinued so resources go to more successful products.

book_ref.quote: This means reviewing the information to find patterns, trends, and insights

blocks.prompt: 6 Define revenue and profit. A shop sells 150 school bags at Rs. 600 each. Its costs are rent Rs. 20,000, salaries Rs. 25,000 and cost of goods Rs. 15,000. Find its revenue and profit. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation: Revenue is the total money earned from selling goods or services. Profit is the money left after subtracting all the costs of running the business (rent, salaries, cost of goods). So find revenue = quantity x price, add all costs, then profit = revenue - costs.

book_ref.quote: Revenue is the total amount of money a business earns from selling goods or services

steps: Revenue = number of bags x price = 150 x 600 = Rs. 90,000
Total costs = rent + salaries + cost of goods = 20,000 + 25,000 + 15,000 = Rs. 60,000

blocks.prompt: 7 Explain investment and savings. A clothing store invests Rs. 80,000 in new inventory and sells it for Rs. 110,000. It also saves Rs. 12,000 every month for 12 months to buy a new machine. Find the profit on the investment and the total savings. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation: Investment is allocating funds to a business or project with the aim of generating future profit; the store expects to sell the inventory for more than it cost. Savings are money set aside for future needs, such as new equipment, expansion or unexpected expenses. So profit = selling amount - amount invested, and savings = monthly amount x number of months.

book_ref.quote: it anticipates selling the items for a higher amount than the cost, thereby earning a profit

steps: Profit on investment = selling amount - investment = 110,000 - 80,000 = Rs. 30,000
Total savings = monthly saving x months = 12,000 x 12 = Rs. 144,000
blocks.final_answer: Profit on investment = Rs. 30,000; savings after a year = Rs. 144,000

blocks.prompt: 8 Define loan and interest. A shop needs Rs. 250,000 for one year. Bank A charges 12% per year and Bank B charges 9% per year. Find the total repayment for each bank and how much the shop saves by choosing the lower rate. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation: A loan is borrowed money (from a bank or another financial institution) that must be paid back with interest. Interest is the cost of borrowing money, usually a percentage of the loan amount. Total repayment = loan amount + interest rate x loan amount; a higher rate means a larger repayment.

book_ref.quote: Example: if a tea shop in Multan takes a loan of Rs. 100,000 at an interest rate of 10% per year

steps: Bank A interest = 12% x 250,000 = Rs. 30,000; total repayment = 250,000 + 30,000 = Rs. 280,000
Bank B interest = 9% x 250,000 = Rs. 22,500; total repayment = 250,000 + 22,500 = Rs. 272,500
Saving with the lower rate = 280,000 - 272,500 = Rs. 7,500
blocks.final_answer: Bank A: Rs. 280,000; Bank B: Rs. 272,500; the shop saves Rs. 7,500 with Bank B

blocks.prompt: 9 Define expenses and budget. A bakery's monthly budget is rent Rs. 150,000, ingredients Rs. 100,000, salaries Rs. 200,000 and utilities Rs. 50,000. Its actual expenses for the month come to Rs. 530,000. Find the total budget and say whether the bakery overspent or saved, and by how much. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation: Expenses are the costs a business incurs while operating, such as rent, utilities, salaries and raw materials. A budget is a plan that estimates how much money will be needed for different areas of the business. Comparing the budget to the actual expenses shows whether the business is overspending or saving money.

book_ref.quote: These can include rent, utilities, salaries, and the cost of raw materials

steps: Actual expenses = Rs. 530,000, which is more than the budget
blocks.final_answer: Total budget = Rs. 500,000; the bakery overspent by Rs. 30,000

blocks.prompt: 10 Communication and storytelling help you express ideas and connect with others. (i) Define communication and explain three things that make it effective when presenting a project. (ii) Define storytelling and explain five tips to develop communication and storytelling skills. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Communication is the process of exchanging information, ideas or feelings with others. It can be verbal (speaking or writing) or non-verbal (gestures or facial expressions). Good communication involves clearly conveying your message and actively listening to others. When presenting a class project on environmental conservation, effective communication involves:
1. Clear speaking: speaking in a manner that is easy for everyone to understand.
2. Good body language: using gestures, maintaining eye contact and standing with confidence.
3. Listening: addressing questions from the audience and considering their feedback.

(ii) Storytelling uses words, images and emotions to create a narrative that engages the audience; a well-crafted story captures attention, simplifies complex ideas and helps the audience remember the message. Tips:
1. Practice regularly: the more you speak and tell stories, the more confident you become.
2. Know your audience: tailor your message to classmates, teachers or family members.
3. Use visual aids: pictures, diagrams and props make the story engaging and easier to understand.
4. Be clear and concise: avoid unnecessary details and focus on the main message.
5. Show emotion: use your voice and facial expressions to show how you feel; this makes communication authentic and relatable.

book_ref.quote: Good communication involves clearly conveying your message

blocks.prompt: 11 Collaboration and iteration help refine ideas and solutions. Define collaboration and iteration with one example of each from the book, and explain their importance using the community clean-up drive example. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
Collaboration: when two or more people work together to achieve a common goal, sharing ideas, resources and efforts to solve problems or create something new. In Pakistan it is seen when students work on a group project or community members organize an event. Example: for a science exhibition model, one student draws diagrams, another builds the model and another explains it; together they produce a better project than any one could alone.

Iteration: repeating a process with the aim of getting closer to a desired result, making changes and improvements based on feedback until the final outcome is achieved (like adjusting ingredients while cooking). Example: a class designs a logo for a school event, shares it for opinions, revises colors and shapes, seeks more feedback and repeats until everyone approves the final logo.

Importance: collaboration and iteration help you produce better results and learn from others. Collaboration pools knowledge and skills to solve complex problems; iteration refines the work, making it better with each step.
Clean-up drive example: community members plan where to start and which areas need most attention. As they work they may find some tasks take longer or more volunteers are needed. They adjust their plans (iterate) and continue working together (collaborate) until the whole area is clean.

book_ref.quote: Collaboration and iteration are important because they help you to produce better results and learn from others

blocks.prompt: 12 Innovation and creativity drive progress. (i) Define innovation and creativity with the book's Pakistani example of each. (ii) Explain four ways to foster innovation and creativity. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Innovation is the process of developing new ideas, products or methods that bring about significant change or improvement. It is not just inventing something entirely new, but also improving existing things to make them better, faster or more efficient. Example: mobile banking in Pakistan. Earlier, people had to visit banks in person, which was time-consuming and inconvenient, especially in rural areas; now they send and receive money, pay bills and manage banking directly from their mobile phones.
Creativity is the ability to think in new and original ways, using imagination to generate ideas that are different from the norm. It is not limited to artists or inventors but is valuable in every field, from science and engineering to business and education. Example: local Pakistani brands use creativity in advertising campaigns that promote their products and forge emotional connections with the audience.

(ii) Ways to foster innovation and creativity:
1. Be curious: always ask questions and explore how things work; curiosity is the first step to innovation.
2. Take risks: don't be afraid to try new things even if they might not work the first time; many successful innovations come from learning from failures.
3. Think outside the box: look at problems from different perspectives; the best solutions may be ones nobody else has thought of.
4. Collaborate: working with others can spark new ideas and lead to innovative solutions.

book_ref.quote: Innovation is the process of developing new ideas, products, or methods that bring about significant change or improvement
